objectives.en: Define the hypergeometric distribution and find its mean

narration.en: How many times must a learner fail the driving test before passing? How many defective bulbs will a sample of 5 from a carton of 20 contain? These two questions lead to the geometric and the hypergeometric distributions.
narration.kn: ಚಾಲನಾ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ತೀರ್ಣರಾಗುವ ಮೊದಲು ಎಷ್ಟು ಬಾರಿ ವಿಫಲರಾಗುತ್ತೇವೆ? 20 ಬಲ್ಬ್‌ಗಳ ಪೆಟ್ಟಿಗೆಯಿಂದ 5 ರ ಮಾದರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಷ್ಟು ದೋಷಯುಕ್ತ ಬಲ್ಬ್‌ಗಳಿರುತ್ತವೆ? ಈ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು ಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ಮತ್ತು ಅತಿಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ವಿತರಣೆಗಳಿಗೆ ದಾರಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: A population of $N$ items has $M$ of one kind (say defective) and $N - M$ of the other. A sample of $n$ is drawn without replacement. The number $X$ of defectives in it has $P(X = x) = \dfrac{{}^MC_x \; {}^{N-M}C_{n-x}}{{}^NC_n}$. Its mean is $\dfrac{nM}{N}$. When $N$ is very large compared with $n$, it is close to $B(n, M/N)$.
body.kn: N ವಸ್ತುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ M ಒಂದು ಬಗೆಯವು. n ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ಮರುಸೇರಿಸದೆ ಎಳೆದಾಗ ಆ ಬಗೆಯವುಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ X ಅತಿಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ವಿತರಣೆ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತದೆ. ಸರಾಸರಿ nM/N.

points.en: Approaches binomial when N is large

narration.en: A population of N items has M of one kind (say defective) and N - M of the other. A sample of n is drawn without replacement. The number X of defectives in it has P(X = x) = dfrac^MC_x ; ^N-MC_n-x^NC_n. Its mean is dfracnMN. When N is very large compared with n, it is close to B(n, M/N).
narration.kn: N ವಸ್ತುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ M ಒಂದು ಬಗೆಯವು. n ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ಮರುಸೇರಿಸದೆ ಎಳೆದಾಗ ಆ ಬಗೆಯವುಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ X ಅತಿಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ವಿತರಣೆ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತದೆ. ಸರಾಸರಿ nM/N.

narration.en: The teacher draws an urn for the hypergeometric case, then a chain of failures ending in a success for the geometric case.

say.en: An urn holds 5 red and 3 white balls. We draw 3 without replacement and count the red ones.
Choose 2 of the 5 red and 1 of the 3 white, out of all ways to choose 3 from 8.
Now the geometric case: keep trying until the first success. X counts the failures before it.
The probabilities fall by a factor q each step, like a geometric progression. Here p is one half.
Mean is q over p and variance is q over p squared.

narration.en: A lot of N items has M defectives; 5 are drawn without replacement. The bars are the hypergeometric probabilities of x defectives; the outlines are the binomial B(5, M/N) for drawing with replacement. For a small lot they differ; as N grows they become the same.

caption.en: A lot of N items has M defectives; 5 are drawn without replacement. The bars are the hypergeometric probabilities of x defectives; the outlines are the binomial B(5, M/N) for drawing with replacement. For a small lot they differ; as N grows they become the same.
caption.kn: N ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಲಾಟ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ M ದೋಷಯುಕ್ತ; ಬದಲಿಸದೆ 5 ಎಳೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಕಂಬಗಳು x ದೋಷಯುಕ್ತಗಳ ಅಧಿಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆಗಳು; ರೂಪರೇಖೆಗಳು ಬದಲಿಸಿ ಎಳೆಯುವ ದ್ವಿಪದ B(5, M/N). ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಲಾಟ್‌ಗೆ ಬೇರೆ; N ಬೆಳೆದಂತೆ ಒಂದೇ.

tryThis.en: With N = 10 and 30% defective, can you draw 4 defectives? What does the binomial say?
Raise N to 200. How close are the two now?
Both have mean nM/N. Which has the smaller variance, and why?

body.en: If independent Bernoulli trials with success probability $p$ are made until the first success, the number of failures $X$ before it has $P(X = x) = q^x p$, $x = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. Mean $= q/p$, variance $= q/p^2$. It is the only discrete distribution with the lack-of-memory property: $P(X \ge s + t \mid X \ge s) = P(X \ge t)$.
body.kn: ಮೊದಲ ಯಶಸ್ಸಿನ ಮೊದಲು ವಿಫಲತೆಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ X ಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ವಿತರಣೆ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತದೆ: P(X = x) = qˣp. ಸರಾಸರಿ q/p, ಪ್ರಸರಣ q/p². ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಸ್ಮರಣೆ ಇಲ್ಲದ ಗುಣವಿದೆ.

points.en: P(X ≥ k) = qᵏ; lack of memory

narration.en: If independent Bernoulli trials with success probability p are made until the first success, the number of failures X before it has P(X = x) = q^x p, x = 0, 1, 2, dots. Mean = q/p, variance = q/p^2. It is the only discrete distribution with the lack-of-memory property: P(X ≥ s + t mid X ≥ s) = P(X ≥ t).
narration.kn: ಮೊದಲ ಯಶಸ್ಸಿನ ಮೊದಲು ವಿಫಲತೆಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ X ಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ವಿತರಣೆ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತದೆ: P(X = x) = qˣp. ಸರಾಸರಿ q/p, ಪ್ರಸರಣ q/p². ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಸ್ಮರಣೆ ಇಲ್ಲದ ಗುಣವಿದೆ.

caption.en: Geometric distribution: failures before the first success. Slide p.

narration.en: Move the success probability. A large p makes zero failures most likely; a small p gives a long, slowly falling tail.

tryThis.en: Set p = 0.5 and check that each bar is half the one before.
Make p small. What happens to the mean?
Is the variance always larger than the mean here?

problem.en: A carton has 20 bulbs, of which 4 are defective. A sample of 3 is drawn without replacement. Find the probability of no defective bulb, and the mean number of defectives.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A carton has 20 bulbs, of which 4 are defective. A sample of 3 is drawn without replacement. Find the probability of no defective bulb, and the mean number of defectives.

problem.en: A learner passes a test with probability 0.4 at each attempt. X = number of failures before the first pass. Find P(X = 2), the mean and the variance.

narration.kn: ತಂಡ ರಸಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ. ನಿಮ್ಮ ತಂಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಮಾಡಿ ಒಂದೇ ಉತ್ತರಕ್ಕೆ ಬನ್ನಿ.

narration.en: Now two questions in the pattern of the II PUC Statistics board exam. Try them on your own first, then check.

points.en: Hypergeometric: sampling without replacement; mean nM/N.
Geometric: P(X = x) = qˣp, failures before first success.
points.kn: ಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ: P(X = x) = qˣp, ಮೊದಲ ಯಶಸ್ಸಿನ ಮೊದಲಿನ ವಿಫಲತೆಗಳು.

points.en: The geometric distribution has no memory.

homework.en: From 10 students (4 girls), 3 are chosen at random. Find the distribution of the number of girls.

narration.en: Recap. Hypergeometric: sampling without replacement; mean nM/N. Geometric: P(X = x) = qˣp, failures before first success. Geometric mean q/p, variance q/p². The geometric distribution has no memory.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಅತಿಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ: ಮರುಸೇರಿಸದ ಮಾದರಿ; ಸರಾಸರಿ nM/N. ಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ: P(X = x) = qˣp, ಮೊದಲ ಯಶಸ್ಸಿನ ಮೊದಲಿನ ವಿಫಲತೆಗಳು. ಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ಸರಾಸರಿ q/p, ಪ್ರಸರಣ q/p². ಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯ ವಿತರಣೆಗೆ ಸ್ಮರಣೆ ಇಲ್ಲ.
